original_value: Display advertising is a $50 billion industry in which advertisers’ (e.g., P&G, Geico) demand for impressions is matched to publishers’ (e.g., Facebook, Wall Street Journal) supply of them. An ideal match is one wherein the publisher’s ad impression is assigned to the advertiser with the highest value for it. Intermediaries (e.g., Google) facilitate this match between advertisers and publishers by managing data and providing optimization tools and algorithms for serving ads. Although these markets exhibit high allocative efficiency, we argue there is considerable scope for improvement.

result.paraphrase: Display advertising is a $50 billion industry where advertisers’ demand for impressions, such as P&G and Geico, is paired with publishers’ supply of them, such as Facebook and the Wall Street Journal. In an ideal match, a publisher’s ad impression goes to the advertiser that values it most. Intermediaries like Google help connect advertisers and publishers by handling data and offering optimization tools and algorithms for ad delivery. Although these markets are highly allocatively efficient, we argue that there is substantial room for improvement.
